# Wharf 0.6.0 image pull and rate-limit research

## Scope

Session 6 adds reusable image preparation for required registry images. It
must inspect the local image store first, coalesce duplicate work, retry only
registry rate limits, and retain complete structured 429 evidence. Derived
image builds, trial containers, and the complete `B` preparation gate remain
Session 7 work.

## Decisions

- Keep image preparation behind a Wharf-owned coordinator with injectable
  Docker, delay, random, telemetry, and console boundaries.
- Use `docker image inspect` for the local-store check and `docker image pull`
  for retrieval. Capture stdout and stderr concurrently and preserve failures.
- Classify HTTP 429, Docker `toomanyrequests`, and explicit registry
  rate-limit responses as retryable. All other pull failures are deterministic
  for this layer and fail immediately.
- Use capped exponential backoff with bounded multiplicative jitter. Track
  registry pressure across pulls, increase it after each 429, and decay it one
  step after successful pulls.
- Coalesce each normalized image reference for the coordinator lifetime.
  A local hit and a successfully pulled image are reused without another
  registry request.
- Write schema-versioned JSONL records for every 429 and atomically replace a
  summary containing total responses, affected images, exhausted retries,
  cumulative delay, and per-image outcomes.
- Keep default console output to one aggregate warning after an affected image
  succeeds or exhausts retries. Emit each retry at verbosity levels 2 and 3.
- Preserve read-only host checks. Address-pool/VPN analysis, ephemeral network
  allocation, and required local-only base-image policy remain preparation
  inputs and are not added to `wharf check`.

## Evidence

- [`docs/wharf-sessions.md`](../../docs/wharf-sessions.md) defines bounded,
  jittered, decaying 429 retries, duplicate coalescing, local reuse, durable
  evidence, and verbosity-sensitive console output.
- [`docs/wharf.md`](../../docs/wharf.md) requires local inspection before
  registry access, forbids a separate pull-concurrency setting, and requires
  deterministic failures not to be retried as rate limits.
- [`docs/wharf.jsonl`](../../docs/wharf.jsonl) traces the slice through
  `CON-078`-`CON-091`, `REQ-105`, `REQ-109`-`REQ-111`, and `AC-011`-`AC-013`.
- Session 5 review defers network mutation and required base-image policy to
  image preparation while keeping host checks read-only.
